Review round 1 (chain exact, head 6412ebf67a37d8bb194a8b9dcfdabe4d6ed08445). Blocking: 4 findings (any finding blocks at round 1-3). Also: this PR touches sensitive paths (`.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/agents/worker-implementer.md`), so it needs a human to approve/merge regardless; nothing was approved or merged.

CI (read per run from statusCheckRollup): "Guards (...)" SUCCESS 13:19:37Z, "Lint, test, typecheck, build" SUCCESS 13:22:19Z, two entries, no skipped run hiding another.
Step 4b counter, run verbatim: `0 exact` (reviewer eiriksf-capgemini, author `app/hal9000-agent-bot`, 0 marker rows). The first bot-authored PR in this repo reads exact, as the PR claims.

**F1 (medium) - worker-implementer.md "same shell" cannot be followed as written, and the failure is silent.** The new block says "Make the commits in a shell that has run the eval" and "Then `gh pr create` in the same shell, with `GH_TOKEN` still set". The file's own machine section says shell state does not persist between Bash tool calls. An implementer who runs the `eval` in one call and `gh pr create` in the next gets an empty `GH_TOKEN`, and `gh` silently falls back to the human login: the PR is authored by the human, the chain reads `approx`, and nothing errors. (The push fails loudly on the empty token; `gh pr create` does not.) Fix: say the `eval` must be the first line of every Bash call that commits, pushes or runs `gh pr create`, and add a post-create assertion that `gh pr view <n> --json author -q .author.login` equals `app/hal9000-agent-bot` (it is currently only mentioned as what it "reads"). dispatch-bead's bullet has the same "set" wording and should carry the same constraint.

**F2 (low) - wrong cross-reference.** step 4b now says "Use the literal author.login you observe in step 3". `author.login` is written down in step 1 (the `--json ...,author` fetch and its bullet); step 3 is the CI gate.

**F3 (low) - unconditioned claim.** "on a bot-authored PR the chain is `exact` whenever author.login differs from gh api user" is false as a sufficient condition: a reset, an `approx` marker, an edited/foreign-author marker or a gap still gives approx/broken (the jq `$broken`/`$reset` branches). State it as "the self-asserted reason for `approx` no longer applies", or list the other conditions.

**F4 (low) - sibling omission, family 4. The PR body says "nothing left"; three same-file statements and four elsewhere still say the old thing:**
- `.claude/skills/pr-review-merge/SKILL.md:620` "in this repo the reviewer and the PR author are the same account" (bootstrap identity-filter bullet).
- same file `:699` "or if its markers were written by the PR's own author (step 4b), which in this repo is every chain until review runs under a separate identity".
- `.claude/skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:149` "What that means in this repo today: the reviewer authenticates as the same account ... every chain reads `approx` and the lenient rounds 4-5 row is currently unreachable" (also says the fix is a separate reviewer bot account; this PR chose the author side).
- `docs/process/development-process.md:340` and `:568` ("Every marker chain is `approx` because reviewer and author share an account ... Fix: ugcportal-62b6, pending on Eirik").
Sweep reach: 5 files scanned (pr-review-merge, review-standards, pre-review, CLAUDE.md, development-process.md) with a regex over same-account/self-asserted/same-login/single-identity/one-account/reviewer-is-author phrases; 21 matches in pr-review-merge (the diff's own file), 2 in review-standards, 2 in docs, 0 in pre-review and CLAUDE.md.

Observation, not a finding: step 4b's argument for why `exact` needs reviewer != author is that anything the reviewing token can write can be forged. The implementer worker still holds the human `gh` login for everything outside the minted-token shell, so a chain on a bot-authored PR is exact by the counter's definition while the human token is still reachable by the implementer. That is the design the bead chose; a human may want to weigh it before rounds 4-5 become reachable for bot PRs.

Verified, no finding:
- K1/K2 greps: gh-app-token/hal9000 present in worker-implementer.md (lines 165-173) and dispatch-bead SKILL.md (89-96); `grep -cE 'normal case|every chain in this repo'` on the skill at head = 0.
- Machine sections of worker-implementer/reviewer/analyst (extracted `## The machine` up to `## Yours in particular`): identical md5 across all three. `git diff 9a94e30 6412ebf -- .claude/agents/worker-reviewer.md` empty (K5).
- #275 (read from GitHub, not the body): author `app/hal9000-agent-bot` (is_bot), sole commit cbbca1fc authored by `hal9000-agent-bot[bot]`, REST `.user.login` = `hal9000-agent-bot[bot]`, one marker comment by eiriksf-capgemini, CLOSED, branch gone from remote. `gh api user` here = eiriksf-capgemini, so the bot is not an alias of the reviewer and the reviewer was not switched (K3/K4/K5). Note the `app/` prefix is a `gh pr view` (GraphQL) rendering; REST gives the `[bot]` form; the new skill sentence scopes itself to `gh pr view`, which holds.
- HTTPS push command: same form as the documented extraheader approach; `base64` on this macOS does not wrap long input (checked with a 290-byte input: 1 line), and the block mentions the pre-push skip and the one-hour token. NOT reproduced: I did not mint a token or run the push/`gh api user` error text (the environment denied minting a credential for me), so "runs exactly" and "`Resource not accessible by integration`" rest on the implementer's report plus the skill's existing step-4b 403 statement.

Families (all four named per angle): (1) F3 and the PR-body "nothing left" claim; (2) F2; (3) no assertions added, nothing to test; (4) F4. Whole-file read (step 4.3) not owed this round (blocking round 1); I read the three changed hunks with their surrounding paragraphs and the full step 4b/5 text, not every line of the 1025-line skill.
